_about: What the port draws for what no level pictures - the portals a shot opens, the shot,
the player, and chapter 1's boss with its spikes - as the original's own entities draw
them. Their images are read from the extracted APK beside the remake and never
Each carries its .ent's <EmissiveColor>, because the original dims every sprite it draws
to min(1, ambient + emissive) of its colour (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117), these as much
And each carries its .ent's lighting facts (step 49, the lighting design's G5): static and
applyLight, which decide which 2D lights reach it (Lighting::ReceiverMask); its <Normal>, a
file under the original's entities/normalmaps/, when it names one; and its <Light>, when it
has one, with the z the light's height is measured from.

_source: A LEVEL PROPERTY rather than an entity. Game's level-properties reader does
CheckCustomData('darkest') and, when it is set, SetAmbientLight(DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT)
- and that single call is the whole of what the flag does in that function.
_moved: The ambient light itself, (0.01, 0.01, 0.01), now lives in lighting.json as
darkest_ambient, where the port's lighting reads it (step 45). The flag is carried on
Game::Level, and the layer multiplies every level sprite by min(1, ambient + emissive)
with that ambient in place of the file's.
Its ONE decoded gameplay consequence is not drawing at all:
canSeeAnything = GetAmbientLight() != DARKEST_AMBIENT_LIGHT, so a minion in a darkest
level is BLIND. minions.json records minion sight as not built. Lighting::Ambient is the
number sight must compare when it lands.

portal._source: the original's portal.ent: Sprite portal_halo.png, blendMode 1 (added), SpriteCut 1 x 1
portal._emissive: portal.ent's <EmissiveColor r=1 g=1 b=1>: min(1, ambient + 1) is 1, so it is never dimmed
portal._lighting: portal.ent: <Entity static=0 applyLight=0>, no <Normal>, no <Light>. Takes no light and gives none

shot._source: the original's projectile.ent: Sprite projectile.png, blendMode 1 (added), SpriteCut 6 x 1, PivotAdjust (4, 0)
shot._emissive: projectile.ent's <EmissiveColor r=0.6 g=0.6 b=1>: under ambient A it is drawn at min(1, A + (0.6, 0.6, 1))
_lighting: projectile.ent: <Entity static=0 applyLight=0>, no <Normal>, and <Particles /> empty, so neither its
light nor its halo is scaled by a particle ratio. <Light active=1 static=0 range=70 haloBrightness=0.65
haloSize=50> with <Position x=0 y=0 z=-12>, <Color r=0.6 g=0.6 b=1>, <HaloBitmap>halo.bmp</HaloBitmap>
(the remake's data_inventory.md, 'projectile.ent'). It has no <Scale>, so the light's offset and
range and the halo's size are the file's own (ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:180-181,
ETHRenderEntity.cpp:378-385). A live light: it reaches every sprite that applies light, static

_note: The shot's own depth, which its light's height is measured from (z + the light's -12). The
script's AddEntity position for projectile.ent is not decoded. 0 is the port's own placement
of the shot, drawn in the player's slot among the art: the player is added at z 0.
How fast the six frames play. The original keeps a _projectileFrameTimer, whose
stride is not decoded.

_source: the original's light_from_projectile.ent, which ETHCallback_light_off adds when a shot lights a torch
(torch.json): Sprite torch_small.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 1 x 1, PivotAdjust (0, -16), one
ParticleSystem of 12 fire.png particles. Since step 55 (the lighting design's G6) only its light and
halo are drawn: its sprite and its flame are not built (torch.json's _not_built).
_lighting: <Light active=1 static=1 range=512 haloBrightness=0.7 haloSize=300> with <Position x=0 y=-12 z=24>,
<Color r=1 g=0.5 b=0.2>, <HaloBitmap>halo.bmp</HaloBitmap>. A STATIC light: in a level that has
not baked at run time it would reach no static sprite, but lighting the torch is what makes the
level bake at run time (Lighting::RuntimeBake), so it reaches every sprite that applies light. Its
halo is scaled by the live share of its 12 particles, which the port does not build: drawn at 1.

_note: The depth its light's height is measured from. The callback's AddEntity position is not decoded
(the bytecode listing was not at hand for step 55); the layer adds it at the torch's own eth_z,
and this value stands only where a torch has none.

character._source: the original's dark_mage.ent: Sprite magic_portals_hd.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 4 x 4, startFrame 4, PivotAdjust (0, 2)
character._emissive: dark_mage.ent's <EmissiveColor r=1 g=1 b=1>: never dimmed by the ambient (what script sets over it is the lighting design's section 5.8, not built)
_lighting: static, so every light reaches it, a static torch's included (ETHEntitySpriteRenderer.cpp:70),
which the remake's fit measured on the original walking past 1-1's torch (fit.md 7.1). Its
lighting height is the level's player marker's eth_z, not a number here.

_note: Which row of the sheet walks which way: derived, not testimony. The original's
DIRECTION enum decodes to MOVING_DOWN 0, MOVING_LEFT 1, MOVING_RIGHT 2, MOVING_UP 3
(the remake's tools/asbc), and Ethanon's own sample picks a character's row by its
direction and its column by a frame timer (Sample-project/main.angelscript:102). The
sheet's row 1 faces left and row 2 right. The owner confirmed on 11 September that the
character turns as it walks; not which rows do it. Rows 0 and 3, arm out, are not
used: the character's `pushing` suggests them, and nothing says when.
How fast it walks through its four columns (the original's frameStride), and which
column it stands on (idleColumn). Neither value is decoded. The start frame, 4, is
column 0 of the left row, the only anchor for the second.

_source: The original's beholder.ent: Sprite beholder.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut 2 x 1. Frame
0 has its eye open and frame 1 shut: ETHCallback_beholder sets 1 while it throws rocks
and 0 otherwise. Its CustomData scale, 0.75, is applied when it appears and replaced
on its first turn: bounce() (utilEntityEffect.angelscript) calls SetScale, which sets
the scale outright (ETHEntity.cpp:601). So it is drawn at its frame's size times its
pulse. The pulse goes from one scale to the other and back by smoothEnd, each way a
stride. While it throws rocks it keeps the last. Its colour is (1, hp / 2, hp / 2).
The original's beholder_spike.ent: Sprite beholder_spike.png, blendMode 0, SpriteCut
1 x 1, PivotAdjust (0, 10). Its image points down, and projectileBehaviour turns it to
where it flies: SetAngle(radianToDegree(getAngle(direction))).
A PLACED entity the level pictures, but drawn as its script redraws it: ETHCallback_portal_static
(Portal.angelscript, bytecode bytes 360571..361404, the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt).
Once, guarded by the uint 'scaled' (ops 1-12, JNZ -> 80 once it is set, ops 17-29 set it):
ops 14-16  thisEntity.Scale(0.8f). ETHEntity::Scale(float) scales the entity AND every particle
system it carries (ETHEntity.cpp:591-599 -> ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:512-518 ->
ETHParticleManager.cpp:444-451, ETHParticleSystem.cpp:27-40, PARTICLE::Scale
ETHParticleManager.h:160-164). The picture is drawn at its frame size times the
scale (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-682): portal_halo.png 64 -> 51.2 u, the rings 110 -> 88.
ops 31-79  SetColor(GetString('color') == 'red' ? vector3(1, 0.3, 0.3) : vector3(0.3, 0.3, 1)).
An AngelScript call pushes its last argument first (the order systems_3_4 read
_portalColorA by, which footage confirmed), so ops 57-59 push z 0.3, y 0.3, x 1: red.
0.3f is PshC4 1050253722 (0x3E99999A). SetColor writes m_v4Color (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498),
which multiplies the SPRITE's min(1, ambient + emissive) (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117);
a particle is drawn in its own colour times ambient alone (ETHParticleManager.cpp:381-389),
so the rings and the iris are not tinted.
A static entity with a callback runs it on every frame its bucket is drawn
(ETHScene.cpp:572 and 488, ETHActiveEntityHandler.cpp:70-74, 90-93 and 145-166), after its particles update.
Footage agrees on the order: red portals read pinker, R/B 0.82 against blue's 0.52 (scripted.md 2.3).
static_portal._not_applied: Scale also scales the entity's collision box (m_controller->Scale). The port's static portal is entered by its trigger_size box, which is gameplay, and is left as it was.

_source: The dial the original adds behind every timed crystal (35 in 20 levels: every inline crystal with a
uint `time`). The original's timer.ent: Sprite timer.png (128 x 64, no hd or fullhd twin), SpriteCut
4 x 2, blendMode 0, static 0, applyLight 0, PivotAdjust (0, 0), Scale 1, no <Light>, no particles.
Cell 0 shows eight wedges and cell 7 one. The script is in the remake's out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt
(md5 48fe65ce...), ETHCallback_crystal.angelscript:
addTimerToCrystal, bytes 424766..425217, called by ETHCallback_crystal when `time` is set:
ins 2-5     g_scale.getScale(), the scale AddEntity gives it: 1 in the port's units
ins 12-25   crystal.GetPosition() - vector3(0, 0, 2): a call pushes its last argument first, so
the 2f of ins 13 is z. The dial stands 2 BEHIND the crystal
ins 29-36   AddEntity('timer.ent', that, the scale)
ins 50-96   its uint `time` the crystal's, `elapsedTime` 0, `crystalID` the crystal's id
ins 100-102 SetAlpha(0.5f)
ETHCallback_timer, bytes 425217..426274, every frame:
ins 1-13    elapsedTime += the frame's milliseconds
ins 53-100  the crystal by its id: gone (taken), elapsedTime += time, which is expiry; there,
SetPositionXY(crystal.GetPositionXY()) - it follows the crystal. The frame it finds
the crystal gone still compares the copy of elapsedTime ins 24-27 took, so it runs
ins 204-252 once more where the dial stood, and the x 0.9 starts on the next frame
ins 102-103 CMPu elapsedTime, time; JNP: while elapsed <= time, ins 204-252; after, ins 105-199
ins 204-231 bounce(this, V2_ONE, vector2(1.15, 1.15), max(400, time - elapsed))
ins 233-252 SetFrame(min(max(int(float(elapsed) / float(time) * 8f), 0), 7))
ins 105-125 SetScale(GetScale() * 0.9f); SetAlpha(GetAlpha() * 0.9f)
ins 127-182 while the crystal is there: AddScaledEntity('crystal_vanish.ent', its position +
(0, 0, scale(20)), scale(1.3)), playCrystalVanishSound, DeleteEntity(crystal). The
crystal goes at its time, with a burst. NOT BUILT HERE: the burst is the visuals plan's
step 10.2, and the sim's crystal already goes (Goals::Crystal::expired)
ins 184-199 GetScale().x < 0.1f: DeleteEntity(this). GetScale is the entity's own scale, which
bounce set as pulse x m_scaleFactor (below), not the pulse: see screen_px_per_unit
bounce, utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes 327057..327527: blinkElapsedTime from 0, taking the same
frame times (ins 1-39); invert = (elapsed / stride) % 2 == 1 in uints (ins 55-61); bias =
float(elapsed % stride) / float(stride), 1 - bias when inverted (ins 63-75); SetScale(interpolate(
scaleA, scaleB, smoothEnd(bias)) x g_scale) (ins 77-102; ins 90-98 the vector2 SGlobalScale::scale, bytes
5878..5975, whose ins 3-8 multiply by m_scaleFactor). smoothEnd, Interpolator.angelscript bytes
313899..313971 ins 1-4, is CpyGtoV4 PIb; MULf; CALLSYS sin: sin(v x PIb), with PIb = 1.570796327f
(Ethanon GameMath.h:40), as Art::Pulse takes it.
timer._emissive: timer.ent's <EmissiveColor r=1 g=1 b=1>: min(1, ambient + 1) is 1, so chapter 4's dark levels draw it as bright as any
timer._lighting: timer.ent: <Entity static=0 applyLight=0>, no <Normal>, no <Light>. Takes no light and gives none
timer._frames: ETHCallback_timer ins 238 (MULIf 8f) and ins 247 (min 7): the time divided into 8 cells, 0 to 7
timer._alpha: addTimerToCrystal ins 100-102, SetAlpha(0.5f). Measured on the original 0.49-0.55 (1-15, 1-27)
timer._z_offset: addTimerToCrystal ins 12-25: the crystal's position less vector3(0, 0, 2). Drawn after the sprites at or below the crystal's z_index - 2 and before the next; the original's library shows the crystal over it
timer._pulse_to: ETHCallback_timer ins 211-217, vector2(1.15f, 1.15f). Measured on the original: a fitted scale of 1.025-1.15
timer._pulse_min_leg_ms: ETHCallback_timer ins 204-208, max(400, time - elapsedTime): each leg of the pulse, which shortens to 400 ms as the time runs out
timer._shrink_per_frame: ETHCallback_timer ins 105-125: scale and alpha each x 0.9f a frame, from the frame the time is up, or from the frame after the one that finds the crystal taken

_note: The frames that x 0.9 is counted in. The script multiplies once a frame whatever the frame's length;
the original's frame rate is not decoded, and the visuals plan's order (00_order K2, the owner's
standing ruling) takes 1/60 s of frame time, the port's tick.

_gone_below_scale: ETHCallback_timer ins 184-199, GetScale().x < 0.1f, on the entity's RAW scale: the port's scale (the pulse,
then the shrink) x screen_px_per_unit. Each frame multiplies (ins 105-125) before it tests (ins 184-199), and
a dynamic entity's callback runs before the frame is mapped for drawing (Ethanon ETHScene.cpp:467-484), with
DeleteEntity taking it out of its bucket at once (ETHBucketManager.cpp:434-460): the frame it goes is not
drawn. So it is drawn shrinking on one frame fewer than the frames it takes to go. From exactly 1: gone on
the 32nd frame, drawn shrinking on 31. From 1.15: the 33rd, 32 drawn. The pulse at which 32 turns to 33 is
_screen_px_per_unit: SGlobalScale.m_scaleFactor, which the dial's scale is stored in. bounce (utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes
327057..327527) ins 90-102 is SetScale(g_scale.scale(the pulse)), and the vector2 SGlobalScale::scale
(bytes 5878..5975) ins 3-8 multiplies by m_scaleFactor; ETHEntity::GetScale returns what SetScale stored
(Ethanon ETHEntity.cpp:601-613). bounce runs on every live frame, the last included (ins 102-103 -> 204-231),
so the shrink starts from pulse x m_scaleFactor whatever AddEntity was given. m_scaleFactor is
m_absoluteSize 256 from main on (00_order 8.12a; view.json's height_px). The screen is 720 px tall by the
owner's standing ruling R12, the fixed 720 selection (as ui.json's speed_at_screen_px), so 720 / 256. The
original's own dial therefore lasted longer on a taller screen; the port takes the 720 one. The port draws
the dial at the pulse in its own units (the cell x scale): only the deletion test takes this factor
